utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. And I think Mr. Vasic now is ready to continue his questions. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Vasic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I hope that you remember my warning to make a pause between my question and your answer so that our cross-examination proceeds smoothly. Yesterday you mentioned you had a work obligation. You must have been familiar with the existence of the Vukovar Crisis Staff and the hospital, or medical centre Crisis Staff in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said yesterday that I was not directly familiar with these, but I was aware of their existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know where these two institutions were physically located in October and November 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified in chief yesterday that until the 16th of November you remained in your flat, after which you went to a shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me if your son was with you in the flat until the 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he join you on the 16th and did he go to that shelter with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you perhaps tell us where he went after the 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I no longer remember, really. But I know that when we reached the hospital on the 19th he was there waiting for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your flat was damaged or destroyed on the 16th, that the building was hit. Why didn't you go to the hospital's atomic shelter but, rather, you chose to dwell in the shelter you told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shelter that I mentioned was for the use of people residing in that neighbourhood. The one in the hospital was for the hospital primarily. That wasn't where I belonged, so in -- that wasn't where I was meant to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, do you know that at one point in time, between September and November 1991, the Vukovar defence Crisis Staff declared a state of general mobilisation in relation to both the regular forces and the reserve forces of the ZNG in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us how and why on the 19th of November you headed for the hospital. What I want to know is, having arrived in the hospital, did you see any members of the ZNG or MUP there, people you might have known?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian army provided the security detail for the hospital, but I knew very few of those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you perhaps drop a name or two among those you did know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you about one who was the one I saw the most often there. He ended up with me in Ovcara. What happened to him later I don't know. His last name was Mikletic and we called him Brko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see or hear that members of the ZNG and MUP in the hospital put on civilian clothes or white overcoats such as were normally worn by doctors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see or hear that in order for their identity not to be revealed members of the ZNG and MUP dressed themselves up in bandages so as to make themselves look as if they were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 19th when you were in the hospital and when the civilians were leaving the hospital, you said that you stayed behind because of your job. What I want to know is did any other people remain there who did not have the kind of job that you had and who were not duty-bound for that reason to stay behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The couple of people I mentioned do belong to that category. But they all worked for the hospital at one time or another. Or else they were family members of someone working in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone from the hospital administration ran any checks to see who stayed in the hospital and who left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that two of the gentlemen you referred to yesterday, Emil Cakalic and Goran Vidos, were members of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Mr. Cakalic. As for Mr. Goran Vidos, what I said is that he came to the hospital during the war to work there as an electrician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to the hospital, did you report to the hospital administration to have your name put on a list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did your name end up on the evacuation list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met up with my son who was there already, and he said that he had put our names on that list, that an evacuation procedure had been agreed for the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he perhaps say when he got to the hospital and when it was that he had put your names on the list, although you weren't there at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't say. I think he arrived one day before we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question by my learned friend yesterday, you mentioned someone named Bogdan Kuzmic. You said he was wearing an old JNA uniform. Was this uniform different from the sort worn by regular JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I did my military service, we used to have this winter-time uniform, olive-drab, made of thick material, and there was a summer uniform, too, also in two colours. Nowadays you have the camouflage uniform and what I now refer to as the old uniform. Not because it was particularly threadbare but because it was more traditional. It was olive-drab and this was the sort of uniform worn in winter normally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign for one of these when you were given your military assignment in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the JNA, but that was 50 years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was precisely my question. When you did your military service with the JNA, because all conscripts signed for these uniforms, all those who were given their military assignment, those who were in the reserve forces, too, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I was a scribe, or a notary in the army. A clerk. And I had no further duties. I was never again called to serve in the reserve forces. Not even temporarily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You recounted for us yesterday a dialogue that you had with a soldier on the morning of the 20th on your way out of the hospital. Apparently he told you that you would now be six feet under had it not been for the great number of Serbian soldiers who had been taken by the Croats. Did he say that you would need to be exchanged in order to get those soldiers of theirs back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't say so explicitly, but I think that was the meaning behind what he actually stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to one of my colleague's questions yesterday, one of my learned friend's questions, you drew a sketch for us to show how exactly the buses were parked on Gunduliceva Street and you showed us the one that you got on. What I want to know is when the buses left the hospital and headed for the barracks and when they got there, which was your bus in terms of the sequence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fourth bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the barracks and arrived at Ovcara, what one was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same sequence as previously at the barracks. That's how we set out and that's how we got there. It was the fourth bus, the one that I was on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned two or three soldiers, as you say, who met you outside the bus; that was before the gauntlet you told us about at Ovcara. Were these two or three soldiers paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've no idea which unit they belonged to, but those were no young conscripts of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got off the bus and passed through that gauntlet, you mentioned a lieutenant colonel who told you to get inside. Can you please describe what this officer looked like, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me now to remember exactly. I know that he wore the standard-issue officer's uniform, olive grey. He had some sort of -- his jacket was not buttoned up to the top, and he wore an officer's cap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your statement to the ICTY investigator? Did you not tell him that you thought he was about 170 centimetres tall, rather plump, with a roundish face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about this lieutenant colonel. Is this the same person that your friend later took you to see when he wanted to get you out of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very dark by this time, and it was difficult to distinguish any shapes. I would say that it was the same person, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday that you heard that the people guarding you inside the hangar were military policemen. Did you ever hear that these were military policemen belonging to the Gradovac [phoen] 18th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea about that brigade. I never heard anything about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Emil Cakalic yesterday. Can you please tell us if he came to the hangar before you arrived or after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was after I arrived. And as I said, there were people lined up along the whole length of the wall, so he was told to stand on top of that hay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was he from the place where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About five metres away, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned events that took place in the central part of the hangar, and in response to a question by my colleague you identified, pointed to two people who had been beaten there, and you said for -- you said one of their names and for the other one you said that you had heard that that was his name. The two people that you mentioned yesterday, Damjan Samardzic, called Veliki Bojler, and Kemal Saiti, do you know if they were members of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. In regard to Mr. Samardzic, but Kemal Saiti was somebody whom I had met in my neighbourhood at the shelter. He had some certain duties there, but he was a plain civilian. He didn't have a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean he had duties within the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I didn't really talk about that with him, so I didn't really know specifically what his duties were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned another person whom you noticed at Ovcara. That was Zarko Kojic. Was he a member of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zarko Kojic also had some sort of function to secure the shelter, and that's from where I know him. This was in my neighbourhood, the same shelter where Kemal Saiti also was. This was also a person dressed in civilian clothes without weapons. At the time he was a young civilian clothes without weapons. At the time he was a young man, under 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when your friend took you out of the hangar, were you the last of that group that you described to be taken out of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you were wearing a watch. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps look to see what the time was when you were coming out of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around 1700 hours. I'm not exactly sure, but that was about the approximate time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look at your watch and see what time it was when you left Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but it was quite dark. You could hardly see anything, and it was just a little bit before 1800 hours when we left Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell the Tribunal investigator that you came to Velepromet at about 1400 -- 1900 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was about 1900 hours when we came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a problem with the question, Your Honours. The answer is fine. The question was: Did you tell the Tribunal investigator that you came to Velepromet at about 900 hours. Answer: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 1900 hours, interpreter's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how long did the trip take from Ovcara to Modateks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About an hour altogether, including stops and also deciding where we would be going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were at the hangar inside and outside of it in Ovcara, did anybody leave the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in front of the hangar, did any vehicle other than the van standing at the distance that you mentioned come and stop in front of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe Mr. Cakalic, what he looked like when you were standing in front of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Cakalic was the person that I was at the hospital with that last night I came to the barracks with him, and also I came to Ovcara with Mr. Cakalic. He was wearing civilian clothes, I know that he had a dark grey jacket, the colour of ice, it was a winter jacket, and he had some sort of a cap. I don't know what it was like. I didn't notice what he was wearing on the lower part of his body. He was wearing just plain civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I meant, but I didn't want to interrupt you so that your voice wouldn't be heard through my microphone. What I'm interested in is in view of the gauntlet that he had to pass, what was Mr. Cakalic's face like, was he bloody, was he wearing glasses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not wearing glasses because the three soldiers in front of the gauntlet who were waiting there and robbing people, one of them took the glasses from him and he stamped on them on the concrete, so he had lost his glasses. He was beaten. It's very hard right now to say exactly how he was beaten and how much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you told us about his glasses, was that something that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you were watching that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stepped out of the bus, one behind the other and we reached the soldiers. Once I was searched and once they had taken what they wanted, I went through the gauntlet, and he stayed behind. He was the next in line, and that was why he was the last one to enter the hangar. During the time that we were together, while I was searched, one of those people who was there took the glasses from his face and he threw them down on the ground and stomped on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, were you searched together or were you the one to be searched first and then him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was searched first and then he was searched, but those two people who were taking the things -- there were two people who were taking the things from us. The third person was just looking on from the side, and he was just doing some other things that needed to be done on top of what these other two people were doing. So that is what this person did to Mr. Cakalic's glasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that moment when they took his glasses, were you standing next to him or were you on the concrete path in the gauntlet or near the gauntlet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the concrete driveway, because that driveway connects to the road. I was in front of him, and he was behind me. Not exactly behind me, but a little bit to the side, so I was able to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were looking at that you were passing through the gauntlet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You couldn't really look at much, as you were going through the gauntlet, but it was much easier during the time that we were being searched and when things were being taken away. At that time, before the gauntlet, it was much easier to see what was happening to us and around us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have another question about the hangar. As you were going inside and you described that it was filling up from the door towards the straw, or was it filling up from the straw to the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hangar was filling up. First you would pass through the gauntlet, then you would go right to the end of the hangar, then left to the end of the hangar, and then again left to the end of the straw. That is the way to orient yourself as you were coming into the hangar and looking at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite clear. What I was asking was, was the start at the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right at the door to the right side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you reached Velepromet, or you came to Velepromet, did you know, did you maybe see or hear that Mr. Bingulac [phoen], a member of the Vukovar TO, was in charge of Velepromet and he refused to accept you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that person, the person who waited for us at the entrance to Velepromet and the person who told the driver that there was no room for us, that he had to drive us to Modateks, the driver later said that that was Mr. Bingulac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people that you mentioned from Modateks, a grand-dad, Dada, and the other person was Velimir Stankovic, were the two of them members of the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said about Jezdimir Stankovic that the first time I saw him was in the barracks and that he was wearing a JNA uniform. Jezdimir Stankovic was not in the hallway where we were situated; he was in the courtyard building which, according to what I know, was that company's administrative building. The other elderly gentleman whose nickname was Dada, grand-dad, was also wearing an olive-drab uniform, a standard JNA uniform dating from my army days. He was there as a sort of coordinator for all the persons who were placed in the hall of that company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in finding out, you explained the uniforms that they were wearing. The uniforms that they were wearing that you used to wear when you were in the JNA, were they different from the uniforms worn by young JNA soldiers in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you. The young soldiers were dressed differently. Some were wearing the standard soldier's uniform, some were wearing newer uniforms that are being worn now in the army. They were not all dressed the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you were taken to Velepromet again from Modateks and that after that in the evening you were taken to the barracks on the initiative of the captain that you mentioned. When you arrived at the barracks, were you given food, water and cigarettes there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there you were placed in a room with no windows. Were you able to see if the other windows, the other rooms had windows that were broken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was midnight, it was dark. It was a large room. I had the impression that the room took up the whole of the building. The window-panes were broken. Not -- not windows, all the window-panes were broken, so it was quite cold in that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this room part of the main barracks building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. It was a building belonging to the Vukovar barracks compound. Exactly where it was located and what its position was, was something that I really couldn't see because it was dark. We were taken to that room directly from the buses, escorted by soldiers, and we remained there until morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to go back to two details concerning Ovcara. You told us yesterday that you heard while you were in the vehicle that one of those who were escorting, that one of the soldiers escorting you, his last name was Vuja [as interpreted]. Do you know if he was of Croat ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that young man. I think that the other soldier addressed him as that. I didn't know the other soldier. There were two soldiers in the vehicle in which we were returned to Vukovar. According to what I know, that last name would belong to somebody who was not an ethnic Croat. As far as I know, in Vukovar such names are by Ruthenians in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the transcript, page 13, line 24, the last name is not Vuja, but Guja.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Guja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second detail concerns the beating that you described yesterday when you were outside the hangar. You heard the beating, you didn't see it, that's what you said. Were the doors of the hangar closed when you heard that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anymore, but it's possible that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we go into private session, please? I have several questions to ask that might reveal the identity of our witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will, for that reason, go into private session while you deal with those few questions, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir, for your answers. Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic. Cross-examined by Ms. Tapuskovic:

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir, P-031. My name is Mira Tapuskovic, and I am one of Mr. Radic's Defence counsel. I am about to ask you a number of questions, sir. Yesterday we talked a great deal, some questions were asked by my learned friend from the OTP, and some questions were asked by my learned friend Mr. Vasic in relation to a large number of statements that you apparently gave, some you signed and some you didn't. The source of information to base our cross-examinations on for the Defence teams is whatever the OTP gives us. We will have to clear up the issue of the statements that you mentioned yesterday. In answer to one of Mr. Vasic's questions yesterday, and Mr. Vasic, as we know, is defence counsel for Mr. Mrksic, you said that you had no idea how this question allegedly -- how this statement allegedly given in Zagreb on the 27th of July, 1992 has now resurfaced, and you said you did not remember giving that statement to begin with. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You might perhaps remember two days ago being asked by my learned friend Mr. Moore from the OTP a question to this effect: He asked you whether you had had an opportunity to read that statement, and whether the statement outlined the substance of your testimony live before this Trial Chamber. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talked to people from the OTP in preparation of your testimony this document that seems to be awarded the status of a statement that you made, was this shown to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Croatian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This statement conditionally speaking - I hesitate to call it a proper statement - has been served on us, both in Croatian and in English. And your signature is nowhere to be seen on either copy. Can you please tell me, sir, the version that you were shown by the OTP, did that version bare a signature, that copy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any explanation offered to you about this? How did the OTP come into the possession of a document that was at the time taken to be your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask the question, perhaps? Did you ask them how they got this statement with your name on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in a straightforward way like that. But I did say I wished to know who the statement was given by, and who delivered the statement to the OTP. I did ask your colleague yesterday, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this ever explained to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to one of Mr. Vasic's questions you mentioned something about going Budapest in July 1992, and you said you did not provide any sort of written statement there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you went there for an interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: An interview took place, yes, that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that this was under the auspices of the Croatian Committee for Missing Persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we go into private session briefly for one question and one answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, did the director of the hospital, Vesna Bosonac, travel with you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She was there on the same business, but we weren't travelling in the same car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consult with Dr. Bosonac prior to your departure for Budapest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you confer with her once you had arrived in Budapest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please make a pause after my question? This is for your own personal safety and also for the benefit of the interpreters, so that my questions and your answers are adequately interpreted. Yesterday you talked about Budapest. You said that on the Serbian side the people present were Starcevic and Stankovic. Can you tell us who represented Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. There was Dr. Ivan Simonovic who headed the government commission. Further, there was Dr. Ivica Kostovic, Dr. Davor, or possibly Dalibor, Strinovic. There was chief secretary of Croatia's International -- or Croatia's Red Cross, a lady whose name I can't remember, and I have no idea right now if anyone else was there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that there was a total of five members in the Croatian delegation, discounting the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't exactly count them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those talks, because that's what you called them, talks, were those bilateral or trilateral talks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may just add something. Mr. Javorski, who was the president of Croatia's Red Cross, as there too. Last name Javorski, the first name escapes me. As for the talks, the talks were lead by Mr. Simonovic on the Croatian side, and Mr. Starcevic was representing what was then still known as Yugoslavia. They determined the agenda, and they decided what would be discussed. The Croatian side spoke and the Yugoslav side spoke and observations were being made about certain occurrences that are also the subject of this trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about a third party being present, possibly. Do you know, and were you perhaps aware of it then that there was a two-member delegation of the International Red Cross present at those talks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were two gentlemen. They were foreigners, sitting at the head of the table. As far as I remember, they did not get involved, they did not take part in the discussion, but they were physically present. I have no idea who exactly they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The talks were being interpreted for their benefit, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me who selected you and the other gentleman you mentioned to go with Mrs. Bosonac and attend these talks in Budapest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who selected us is not something that I can say. I suppose we were selected because we were victims and eye-witnesses. And we happened to be staying in Zagreb at that time. I was personally informed by Vesna Bosonac, she said that I had been asked by this committee to go and also asked whether I was willing and prepared to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to you told us about your interview with investigator Dzuro. Under some quite strange circumstances during your talk with Mr. Dzuro, you said that you were disappointed about the way you were treated by this commission in Budapest in your capacity as a witness. Can you please tell us what the problem was in the way you were treated as a witness in Budapest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's like this: Our Croatian side brought out the truth and information about the suffering relating to the Vukovar Hospital. The other side was using every opportunity to dispute that, asking for additional explanation with proof that it was or wasn't like that. There was a dominant feeling that some people were telling the truth and others where not really believing that truth completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The investigator Dzuro, regarding these notes, and it was more that -- we're talking about notes, since you said that it was just an interview, that he put some something in the notes that you did not say in the introduction to these notes from June 1999. Other witnesses are mentioned, witnesses, plural. Are you sure that you went -- you were the only people who went to Budapest, you and the gentleman who you mentioned? Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I wrong then in concluding that you actually provided one official statement, that's the statement from April 1996, which you signed, and you gave that to the same investigator, Mr. Dzuro. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I agreed to give a statement that I would acknowledge is my own and which I would sign, Mr. Dzuro used a lot of the conversations from that prior statement that I didn't sign as a way to just remind himself of certain things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you again talked with representatives of the Prosecutor's office in preparation for this testimony, were you again shown that official note, which is also in the same form of a statement, as well as this statement which was signed by you? Were you shown both of those things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were shown to you in the Croatian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, could you make a pause between answer and question. Did you manage to see, other than the introductory part, that those two statements are practically identical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yes, but the expressions and terms used are much more free, or much improvised compared to the official statement that I gave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't have any remarks about this identicalness of these two statements, even though you said that you refused to sign it because there were the stories there were a little bit elaborated or more freely interpreted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I just said. And if I may add, I did not refuse to sign. We agreed at the start of our interview that that would not be an official statement that I would sign or that it would be a statement with which I would take part in any kind of evidentiary proceeding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you said that you did not provide a statement to any of the Croat organs, I'm coming back again to that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a written statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk with any representatives of the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there were representatives of the Croatian government or not. I think one time they were, but there were several such interviews or conversations where we tried to help someone to gain more insight into exactly what happened in the Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that those conversations of your stories, statements were ever part of any kind of official report of any international organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, I never saw that. And nobody showed me anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be more specific now. Did you ever hear that the UN expert commission used information of the health ministry of Croatia, the information department and in its report on the Vukovar Hospital and the Ovcara mass grave site in 1993 mentioned you as a witness and as a source of information based on which the report was drafted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day before, in response to the Prosecutor's questions, you said that -- or you confirmed that you took a small plastic package with you, where all of your statements were. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day before, in answer to a question by my learned friend Mr. Moore, you said that you had with you a plastic envelope, case, cover, where you keep all your statements.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how many of your statements exactly are there in that plastic sleeve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My statements number 1, number 2, number 3 and number 3A are in that sleeve. That's the addendum that Mr. Dzuro made concerning the reasons why I did not appear before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you gave those statements -- and you brought them in agreement with the Prosecutor during your preparation for this testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were -- they are sorted according to the time period when they were compiled.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would this perhaps be an appropriate moment to take a break? Because of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour, I will continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we are going to focus on the events from 1991. Could you please tell us, since the wounded and the ill persons were moved in the basement of the shelter, could you please tell us where you were working? I would just like to remind you, because you are under protective measures, to -- not to tell us exactly what you were doing, but just to tell us where the premises were where you happened to be.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The premises were separate from the hospital complex. They were separated by a city street. And there were three or four buildings there. They were all just single-storey buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to the hospital on the 19th in the early morning, at about 9.00 in the morning Vesna Bosonac came up to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to me, but to all of us who happened to be gathered in the hospital entrance-hall. Like I said in the beginning, there was a lot of staff who had come from the shelter in my neighbourhood and also many from the surrounding buildings around the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And she told you then that you were not supposed to have come to the hospital. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And regardless of the fact that she told you where you were supposed to gather, you remained in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stayed at the hospital because I had already been placed on the list of people to -- meant to leave Vukovar and also I was a part of that medical institution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew Vesna Bosonac personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a physician, yes. Also as a -- the director who was acting director in July 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to see if your name was really on that list for evacuation? Did you talk with her about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't really talk to her on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said that you spoke with her on the 19th in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not speak to her. She addressed us, and she said something about us having or not having to be at the hospital and then she said that all the civilians would, in the course of the day, be taken to the Velepromet collection point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, sir, could you speak a little bit more slowly, and could you make a pause between my questions and your answers, because we are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether you were told at the time, or whether that person had perhaps told you who had come to the shelter where you were whose name you don't know, who was organising the evacuation of the Vukovar population or, rather, the sick persons from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have any such conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me who told you that you and your wife may stay at the X-ray room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My acquaintances, my friends, my colleagues, who were employed at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you allowed to do this, because it was already known on that day that the evacuation would not proceed, that you would stay at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really tell you specifically, but just before nightfall we were looking for a place in the hospital where we could spend the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day before you told us that the family members of the medical staff as well as aides were permitted to stay in the hospital. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who approved this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when this was approved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to the X-ray room with your wife and with all your things, were there any patients in the X-ray room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was a preparatory room where people were prepared for X-rays, using the appropriate machinery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief you said that you knew that the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the director, Mrs. Bosonac, were staying at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening on the 19th until the morning on the 20th of November, yes, they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Emil Cakalic was also there with his wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also the family of the Ivankovic X-ray technician?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and also the radiology technician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The wife -- the husband of Beba, the head nurse, was also at the hospital, Mr. Mihajl Kolesar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. He probably -- no, not probably, he was definitely there, but I don't know where he was staying, but he went through exactly the same thing that I did through the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was also this man who was 17 years old, Tomislav Baumgertner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was there somewhere with his mother, but I don't know in which room he was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were Bucko, Mara and Irinej as well? You know her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Bucko, Mara. I know her husband slightly from seeing him around town. Mara Bucko was a member of staff of the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the mother-in-law of Dr. Njavro was also at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time that I'm hearing about that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Tomislav Selibaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know who Tomislav Selibaj is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us about some other family members of employees whom you saw on the 19th or about whom you knew that they were staying in the hospital even before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I already said that the last eight or ten days I was no longer staying at the hospital because of the situation. Because of the war, it was dangerous to travel anywhere at that time. I don't know about these families that were allegedly staying there. It was probably during that period when I wasn't staying there, so I don't know anything about that, and I couldn't really tell you anything specific about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you saw Martin Dosen lying down in the corridor between the orthopaedics and the urology departments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, between those two specialist wards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I conclude that the doctors, the medical staff and many members of their families were all accommodated, in the rooms in the various shelter rooms, while the wounded and the sick persons were all placed in corridors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have to agree or disagree. It's possible that it was that way, but I really don't know whether it was or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned Bogdan Kuzmic as having entered the X-ray room and that he was looking for some people with two soldiers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was specifically looking for Milicko Vukovic and Zeljko Batarelo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please describe those two soldiers who were with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't interrupt. It's for your own safety. Were they wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have weapons? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the two soldiers were carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a convenient time, is it, Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I think that it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because of a commitment during the break we will take a little longer than usual time and resume at about five minutes to the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You said today in answer to one of my learned friend Vasic's questions something about some persons. I hope we don't need to go into private session. We will not be mentioning their names, but you will remember who I am talking about. You said that this person was not a member of the ZNG, but rather a member of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me when the Croatian army was established? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again I must warn you to make a pause, wait for the interpreter to stop interpreting my question, and then answer, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at this time a reserve officer of the Croatian army or a reserve officer of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both today and yesterday, yesterday this is on page 28 of the transcript, line 14, you mentioned Croatian soldiers who were in charge of the hospital security. Can you please say how many such soldiers were there providing security for the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number. I didn't know. However, as far as I was able to see those were for the most part soldiers standing at the hospital entrances. Around the building itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many entrances did the hospital have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main entrance and across the way from there there was another one. Outside that entrance was yet another one through which you could reach the women's ward, and then there was another door to the pharmacy and the pathology ward. From the front side, and there were several steps there on the way in, there were no soldiers guarding that particular entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, you have used the term "soldiers" while saying that they were not at that particular door. What about the security detail? Did it comprise people who, as you say, were Croatian soldiers, members of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who had them deployed there, or under whose command they were. I never learned, I never talked to any one of those soldiers about it. They were wearing uniforms and they belonged to the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they stand guard there day and night, around the clock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that they were there during day-time. I don't know about night-time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please try to describe the uniforms they had, what colour, what sort of insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't describe the uniforms. I'm not sure that my description would be entirely accurate, as my memory is no longer as fresh as it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us if they were black, olive-drab, blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them were the military colour, olive-drab.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us please go back to the part where you told us about the hospital, about you getting on that bus and about when you were asked to show your IDs. Can you please list all the other hospital employees who had valid IDs and who got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For this reason, because we are about to name names, can we please go into private session, briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you specify at what time exactly the buses left the hospital for the barracks, the Vukovar barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took quite a while, but if I remember correctly that was about 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that at this time there were two soldiers on the bus with you, and one lieutenant. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two soldiers with the driver, the bus driver. However, when and how the lieutenant got in, I didn't see, myself. When we reached the barracks the lieutenant got off the bus and that was when I first laid eyes on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe him for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I could. I was towards the rear of the bus, and he got off the front door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you not even describe his uniform for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in a detailed fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us a great deal about those two groups of persons who surrounded the buses in the yard of the barracks. Can you tell us about those two groups, one of which you referred to as the aggressive group, the other group being reservists, or possibly TO members? At any point in time during your time in the barracks yard were those two groups communicating mutually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them communicating, but I don't think so. I don't think they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the group comprising aggressive persons headed for -- towards the sixth bus which turned up about half an hour after you got there, did they thereupon go to your buses, the buses that you were on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see an officer there who perhaps issued an order for the buses to get going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to that sixth bus? Did that bus join you on the way out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that at the time. I do know now, because I learned after the war upon my return to Zagreb, that the sixth bus was never seen again and nothing is known of the fate of the prisoners who were on that sixth bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those two soldiers who you mentioned were with you on the bus and the lieutenant, did they continue the journey with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those two soldiers never got off the bus at all and they remained with us throughout, all the way to Ovcara. I don't know about the lieutenant. I don't remember. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived outside the hangar at Ovcara, you say the wounded were made to run the gauntlet too, persons who were ill, hospital employees as well as Croatian soldiers who had been in charge of the hospital security. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among those persons, you saw members of the army securing the hospital. Can you give us an approximate number, how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say what the distance was between the two -- the sides of the gauntlet along that concrete driveway leading from the road to the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could Defence counsel turn off the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was approximately the same width as the entrance door to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how wide the door is? We can hardly be expected to use the sketches you made yesterday to assess that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't take any measurements. But the door is wide enough for a piece of agricultural machinery to be introduced through it into the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you described for us what happened to Kemal and Damjan. According to your story's chronological sequence, the way you explained this to us, my conclusion was you were facing the wall at this point in time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How then were you able to see what was going on with Kemal and later on with Damjan if indeed you were facing the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've explained this. I said that I stole a glance out of the corner of my eye and that I could see very clearly what was happening to Kemal. As for Mr. Samardzic, I couldn't see as clearly, but my fellow victims told me that he had met the same fate as Kemal before him. The distance between Kemal and myself was very small.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain what you said about the details yesterday? They were insufficient details, apparently. What exactly was the distance between Kemal and yourself and what do you mean by stealing a glance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How I might explain that to you? You just cast a sideways look, and your angle of vision expands at that moment. There were no soldiers standing behind my back, not near enough anyway, so I was free to turn my head just slightly and see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you came out of the hangar and when you were waiting in front of the hangar with the others, you said that you heard a whistle, the sound of a whistle blowing coming from the hangar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did that sound mean to you at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't mean anything to me, but it explained the following: At the sound of the whistle some of these paramilitary soldiers were leaving the hangar and the others were coming in. The conclusion was that they were conducting beatings because you could hear the sounds, and also the wails of the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that to you the whistle signified a shift in the beatings, but that was a conclusion, you didn't see that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly as I said. One group was coming into the hangar and the other one was leaving the hangar, meaning that there was a shift occurring with the beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It meant only a shift; one group of people was coming in and another group was leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement that you signed you said that you were informed that you wanted to go to Croatia because the transport, the evacuation was supposed to be conducted in two different ways. Those who came to the hospital would go to Croatia, and those who came to Velepromet would go to Serbia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A small correction, not those who went to Velepromet. There was a division there also according to the ethnic membership. It depended on who was a member of what ethnic group, and where they would go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time that you heard about the option that those who would be going to Serbia would go to Sid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few days before the fall. I said in my explanation that we were already in the shelter and that we had already made groups in the shelter and made lists of who would go in what bus. I assume that those who had slightly more power there had certain information already about the pending end of the occupation of Vukovar, that there would be an evacuation according to what the population chose. It was thought that it would be impossible to continue life in the destroyed Vukovar and that it would be necessary to leave.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who were leaving Vukovar, wherever they were going, had to go through Sid. They would even go as far as Sremska Mitrovica, and then they would come back from Sremska Mitrovica, and then they would go to Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia, wherever they wanted to go. So not thinking of the worst that would happen, we felt that we would be leaving the travail of Vukovar, and we would be going to some better place and stop briefly at a place where we then could decide to go, to a better place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for explaining the route that you took. You mentioned Dzo and how one of the officers told him that he would guarantee your security as well as the security of all those who left the hangar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether Dzo went with you in that jeep towards Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was next to the jeep before we left, and he told us to wait at Velepromet until the following day at noon. If he didn't arrive by 12.00, we were free and we should catch the first available bus to Sid. I was even thinking that he was perhaps riding in the front with the driver and Mr. Cakalic, but Mr. Cakalic told me that he wasn't, that it was actually just one of the regular soldiers, just like the two soldiers who were escorting us. After that day I never saw Mr. Ivankovic again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you talked about Dzo Ivankovic as a major in the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how he introduced himself to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday when you were describing the events in the hangar and in the front of the hangar you mentioned a lot of ranks, majors, lieutenants, lieutenant colonels. Did you manage to check the epaulets on those people and did that correspond to how certain people who were present addressed those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were talking amongst themselves, these soldiers, and I didn't have the opportunity to see the officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned the lieutenant who came up to the tractor to be able to see better because the headlights of the tractor were on, can you explain that a little better?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't mention any lieutenants, I would like to correct you. Mr. Ivankovic told us I have to take you inside near the tractor to the major, and then he talked to this major and gave the major the lists he had made of all of us who had been taken out of the hangar. The major signed the list and allowed him to take us back after making the remark that you mentioned. I was not able to see the officer because Mr. Ivankovic and soldiers were standing in the way, but he was standing near the front right headlight, and he was there so that he could read the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I because wanted a description of him. I'm sorry if I made a mistake in his rank, but we both understand each other very well as regards the actual person I'm talking about, and I thank you for your assistance. I have another question. You said that a total of seven of you came out of the hangar who were supposed to be returned to Vukovar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you say if I were to tell you that the report of the UN expert commission dating from 1993, which I mentioned before to you, states that the total number actually was 10 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say anything, because I don't know about that piece of information. However, I do have information that one young man was brought out who was 16 years old, somebody took him out in a similar way, but he was brought back inside when it was discovered that his father was in the Croatian army. This was -- actually, this meant that in my group where I was, there were actually eight people. If anybody said 10, then they are probably counting the soldier who jumped out of the tractor-trailer on the way from the hangar to the execution location and probably the soldier who was in Belgrade for a trial who said that, first of all, he was sent from Bjelovar as a military police officer to the Yugoslav People's Army, then that he escaped to the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We need to cut the answers short, because we have to take into account the time that we have at our disposal, so I would like you to stick to the question. All I asked you was that would you allow for the possibility that there were more people, that there were 10 people as it is stated in the official report of the United Nations? Your answer to that was no, so I thank you for your answer. When you mentioned the "stolarija" room, the carpentry room, the carpenter's room, when was the first time that you heard the term "death room"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I heard it was when I was in that room. People who were in that room before me were talking about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have just one more question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came to Sremska Mitrovica where you were interrogated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give a statement there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, one written statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Tapuskovic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please. Good day, Your Honours, good day to everyone in these proceedings. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, His Honour, the Presiding Judge Parker already said my name. I am attorney Novak Lukic, and I am representing Mr. Veselin Sljivancanin and I will be putting some questions to you now. Could you please pay attention to the break that we need to make, the pause between question and answer, not only because of the interpreters, but also because of the security measures, so please pause before you begin answering my question. The first topic that I would like to ask you about concerns some of the answers that gave to Ms. Tapuskovic, and which I also read in your statement. And you repeated the statement also from your statement concerning your conversation with Dr. Bosonac on the 19th when you arrived at the hospital. Today I actually heard you say that she addressed you. When you came you repeated what you already stated previously in your statement, how she told you that you should not have come there. I assume that she was addressing the group of the citizens who happened to be at the hospital, but that you should have gone to the Velepromet location. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To be more specific, this was around 9.00 a.m. on the 19th of November. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately it was after 9.00, but before 10.00, so between 9.00 and 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She personally addressed the group of citizens where you also happened to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she tell you who should go to Velepromet and why, why to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She said that only those who had some -- something to do with the hospital could stay in the hospital. All other citizens, according to the instructions that she had, were supposed to go to the Velepromet collection point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that during the day you were inside the hospital and outside. I don't want to put anything to you, but did you proceed to the X-ray room immediately, or did you spend sometime during the day inside the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly the time-frame anymore, but I moved around in that area where we were, we were talking amongst ourselves, the people who knew each other. And then in the afternoon or towards evening I tried to find a spot where we could spend the night. So later when it was evening, when it was dark, I came to the room where I actually did spend the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the name Zeljka Zgonjanin mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of Zeljka Zgonjanin. I know her and I know who she was after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information that she or anyone else was compiling a list of the people who were supposed to move to Velepromet? I'm talking about the civilians now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether those people were actually transferred to Velepromet during the day, afternoon or that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And according to you, these are the people who Dr. Bosonac told that morning that they were supposed to go to Velepromet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already answered a question that actually connects to the next topic. You actually said that it was already dark when you arrived at that room where you spent the night, the room next to the X-ray room, and you mentioned who was with you that night. My question is as follows: During that evening from the point when you entered the X-ray room until the morning when you left the room, did you, in that period, leave the room at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point I did. I went to the shelter connected to the hospital to get some water. I had a bottle with me. On my way there, I met a cleaning lady who had worked at the hospital for many years, and I asked her if there was anything to eat anywhere, because at the shelter where I was for two days before that we were not given anything to eat. In those 15 or 20 minutes -- or after 15 or 20 minutes I returned to the X-ray room again, and then I didn't leave it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said that Mr. Kuzmic entered that room at about 9.00 p.m., approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if any of the people who were with you in that room left the room during the evening or night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can recall is that Mr. Milicko Vukovic went out because he was an X-ray technician or a radiology technician. He was working there, so he had contacts with the other staff who were working in the X-ray section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're going to move to a different topic, and what I'm most interested in are the events on the 21st of November, 1991. You described that in the morning they came into the room and told everyone to leave the room and, as you have said, you went towards the exit. What I'm interested in is something else. When you talked about all of those people who had spent the night of the 20th with you at the hospital, you mentioned some names of doctors. What happened to them at the point in time when you left the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two ways that those who were found in the hospital were treated. There were those persons calling upon us to leave the hospital. I didn't see them. I can't say they were military men or civilians. I just heard voices calling upon us to leave the hospital. Then the medical staff had been told to go to the surgery unit and the plaster room. Where plaster-casts were made for those injured. All the medical staff were told to assemble there to see what they would do next and in order to prepare for the evacuation. All those who were non-medical staff who were found in those rooms were told to leave the hospital and go out to the hospital yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
